_comment: Authoring anchors for NEW CED Unit 1 (Exploring One-Variable Data & Collecting Data; OLD topics 1.x + 3.x). Describe what a DOK-2 and a DOK-3 look like here so 66 authors rate by the same yardstick (spec §1.1-1.2). Anchors DESCRIBE released-FRQ patterns; they never quote an item.

dok2_anchors.shape: Given one display, describe shape / center / variability / unusual features in context with units.
dok2_anchors.why_dok2: Multi-feature procedure with one path; the student applies SOCS, no judgment between alternatives.

dok2_anchors.shape: Compute a summary (median, IQR, z-score, percentile) from a table or list and state it in context.
dok2_anchors.why_dok2: Known procedure, single answer; 'show your work' does not raise the level.

dok3_anchors.shape: Two plausible descriptions (or two displays, or two summaries) of the same data; decide which a reader should trust, cite the specific features that settle it, and say what you would report.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: Requires coordinating several features against competing claims and defending a choice; more than one feature is relevant and either claim can be partly defended.

dok3_anchors.shape: A dataset and two claims made from it; decide which claim the data can actually support and what additional data the other would need (intro / sampling / bias days).
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: Bounds a conclusion: the student must distinguish a descriptive statement from an inferential one and name the missing evidence.

dok3_anchors.shape: Two students got different values for a statistic from the same data; find whose procedure is right AND explain what the wrong value would lead a reader to conclude.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: Error analysis plus consequence; the 'so what' requires reasoning about the reader, not just the arithmetic.

not_dok3: A DOK-2 description with more bars, more decimals, or a nastier dataset (R2: DOK is not difficulty).
A DOK-3 whose decision is pre-made in the stem ('Ben is right; explain why') — that is DOK-2 (R3).
Lettered parts that each have exactly one procedure and never ask for a judgment.
